sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source belongs to the Southern Alps most external, S-verging thrust front buried in the Lombardia plain and has been established within the research developed during the European Project GeoMol (http://www.geomol.eu/).
The main element used for the interpretation of the geometry of the seismogenic sources in this sector of the Po Plain is the occurrence of two main detachment layers within the stratigraphic succession cut by the Southern Alps thrust faults. The two detachment horizons are a deeper one located at the top of the Triassic evaporites (or base of the Mesozoic carbonatic sequence), and a shallower one located at the base of the Gonfolite foredeep deposits. The latter in the area between Milano and Mantova, becomes shallower eastward following the shallowing geometry of the basin that hosted the sediments. As a consequence of the presence of the two detachment horizons, the outer front of the Southern Alps is characterized by a major deep thrust cutting through the Mesozoic carbonatic sequence, and by shallow thrusts that developed within the Gonfolite foredeep deposits. The practical outcome for the seismogenic sources interpretation, is that the outer Southern Alps thrust front is now interpreted as being segmented down-dip with separate sources: one corresponding with the deeper thrust, and two with the shallower thrusts, forming two small arcs. The latter, since their detachment is shallowing eastward, have also a reduced down-dip width in the same direction (with important implications on their seismogenic potential, i.e. maximum magnitude of the potential earthquake).
This Composite Source is the easternmost and smaller one of the two shallow structures.
Current earthquake catalogues show a sparse distribution of minor seismicity in this region.
The strike of this Source was taken from the general orientation of mapped tectonic structures; the dip was taken from subsurface evidence of the thrust plane; the rake was assumed to represent pure thrusting, based on general geodynamic considerations. The minimum and maximum depth were based on subsurface geology and on the uncertainty concerning the depth at which active thrusting is rooted. The slip rate was inferred from regional geodynamic data.
